scenes.title: From fraud alert to reviewable decision.
scenes.caption: FRAUDLOOP connects transaction evidence, historical cases and bank policy in one investigation workflow.

scenes.title: Start with the cases that need review.
scenes.caption: The queue brings verdicts, uncertainty, SAR recommendations and pending approvals into one place. These 20 benchmark outputs have all passed validation.

scenes.title: One alert. A connected investigation.
scenes.caption: HHG-014 starts with an analyst request about a shared device profile. The case preserves the trigger, affected transactions, evidence and investigation timeline.

scenes.title: Explore connections beyond one transaction.
scenes.caption: The scoped episode contains 26 transactions across 20 card groups, with $3,778.14 exposure. Nine groups lack authoritative card IDs and remain explicitly unresolved.
scenes.footer: Local graph view · Historical case evidence · No new graph write

scenes.title: Count independent evidence carefully.
scenes.caption: Correlated signals are capped within evidence families. A shared device or a high alert score alone does not decide fraud. The displayed probability is an evidence heuristic.

scenes.title: Read the historical precedent.
scenes.caption: Analysts can inspect confirmed bank outcomes and their narratives. These preserved answers predate detailed rank provenance, so the console labels those missing measurements.

scenes.title: Make the approval route explicit.
scenes.caption: HHG-014 recommends a card block and suspicious activity report with L2 review. Initial and final recommendations remain visible. No card was blocked and no external report was filed.
scenes.badge: BLOCK CARD · L2 / FILE REPORT · L2
scenes.footer: Bank actions are recommendations · SAR draft requires L2 approval

scenes.title: Verification can clear an alert.
scenes.caption: In HHG-002, explicitly simulated customer confirmation changes suspicion from about 43% to 4%. Verification and monitoring become CLOSE NO FRAUD, with zero final exposure.
scenes.footer: Simulated response · Saved benchmark result · Not an observed customer reply

scenes.title: A transaction becomes a review.
scenes.caption: The simulator replays supplied historical transactions. For this local demonstration, a disclosed 0.25 threshold admits transaction 3478782. The alert score opens review; policy decides the outcome.
scenes.footer: Local demo · Threshold 0.25 · No transaction graph writes

scenes.title: Keep the alert reason with the case.
scenes.caption: The alert links directly to its investigation. The feed is bounded to five transactions per second, with one active investigation and at most ten waiting jobs.
scenes.footer: Historical-data simulator · Local mode · No bank action executed

scenes.title: Pause when authorization is unresolved.
scenes.caption: The investigation saves its assessment and asks for customer validation. The request explains why more evidence is needed and shows the precedent basis while it waits.
scenes.footer: Local demo · Analyst input is attributed evidence, not authenticated customer contact

scenes.title: Record the response and its source.
scenes.caption: Here the demo analyst records a customer denial. The response retains the selected L1 role and timestamp. This is a demonstration entry, not a real customer communication.
scenes.footer: Demonstration evidence entry · No customer was contacted

scenes.title: Reassess the same investigation.
scenes.caption: The recorded denial changes the verdict from uncertain to fraud. CREATE CASE is automatic; BLOCK CARD requires L1 approval. The console explains exactly what changed.
scenes.footer: Local execution · Graph write false · Card block remains a recommendation

scenes.title: Control what retrieval brings into context.
scenes.caption: GraphRAG exposes index weights, precedent counts, graph depth, time windows and similarity cutoffs. Each investigation freezes its settings, including while waiting for human evidence.
scenes.footer: Enabling an index uses available coverage · It does not create embeddings

scenes.title: See why a precedent was retrieved.
scenes.caption: Rank fusion combines available vector indexes with graph, pattern and narrative matches. This local preview shows each source's rank and contribution, without inventing vector scores.
scenes.footer: Local preview · Available graph and text matches · No narration or graph writes

scenes.title: Inspect the exact narration context.
scenes.caption: The inspector reveals the compact evidence brief prepared for the language model. Policy code owns verdicts and actions; optional model narration must stay within those decisions.
scenes.footer: No LLM was called for this preview · This demo uses template narration

scenes.title: Consequential actions stay reviewable.
scenes.caption: Viewers can inspect recommendations. L1 and L2 roles expose their allowed review controls, and decisions have an audit trail. The role switcher is a local demo mechanism, not authentication.
scenes.footer: No approval was submitted during capture · No external action executed

scenes.title: Remember outcomes with their provenance.
scenes.caption: Confirmed historical bank outcomes remain distinct from earlier agent conclusions, which may include simulated replies. Retrieval is bounded by each case's opening time.

scenes.title: Preview data before committing it.
scenes.caption: The Data page separates preview from supervisor commit. Transaction rows must match the supplied dataset. Native policy commits use the BGE index; local uploads remain staged.
scenes.footer: Import controls shown only · No data upload or graph migration performed

scenes.title: Twenty answers. Explicit uncertainty.
scenes.caption: All 20 saved answer files pass schema, identifier, exposure, chronology, route and policy validation. These are validated output counts, not an accuracy claim.
scenes.footer: Saved benchmark results · Validation is not accuracy against a hidden answer key

scenes.title: Evidence first. Every decision reviewable.
scenes.caption: Explore the case queue, replay an investigation, and inspect the evidence behind every recommendation.
scenes.footer: TigerGraph HHGOA · FRAUDLOOP · Local walkthrough with simulated/demo evidence
